subject: Acceptance criteria & MAP: Caspian Health pilot checkpoints
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@caspianhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acceptance criteria & MAP: Caspian Health pilot checkpoints

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is a working mutual action plan (MAP) and an initial acceptance-test matrix I pulled together so we can align on what "success" looks for the 6-week pilot. High level:

- Objective: validate Redwood inference for claims triage at 95th‑percentile latency <= 300ms and 85% core-case recall on our seed prompt set.
- Exit gates (pass to production): performance (latency/throughput), quality (recall/precision on the eval set), security checklist completed (SOC2 evidence + ingress/egress controls), and a signed SOW.
- Suggested owners: Caspian product owner (validation), Caspian procurement (contracts), Redwood (runtime ops & evidence).

Key milestones in sheet: kickoff (week 0), smoke tests (week 1), mid-pilot review (week 3), acceptance run (week 5), sign-off (week 6). Each milestone includes explicit acceptance tests and who verifies them.

Can you confirm:
1) the people who will run acceptance (names/roles)?
2) any hard blockers for data/path residency we should account for?
3) whether procurement needs a separate evidence packet beyond SOC2 (e.g., encryption attestations)?

I've attached: Caspian_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP + timeline) and acceptance_test_matrix.csv (test rows + pass/fail criteria).

Attachment stubs: [Attachment: Caspian_MAP_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)] [Attachment: acceptance_test_matrix.csv (text/csv)]

If that looks reasonable I'd propose a 30‑minute alignment call on Tue or Wed this week to lock owners.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0123

Date: 2026-05-24T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance criteria & MAP: Caspian Health pilot checkpoints

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear plan and the artifacts. Quick answers from our side:

1) Owners: I'll be product owner for validation (Emily Zhao). Procurement (copied) will drive contract and evidence intake (Tara Mills, procurement). Engineering (internal) will own smoke tests — I'll add names once I sync with them this afternoon.
2) Data residency: pilot data will stay in our US tenant; we need confirmation on where logs and derivative telemetry are stored and retention policy.
3) Evidence: procurement will want SOC2 report (fine) plus a short one‑pager on network isolation and a KMS integration note.

Couple of comments on the MAP:
- The latency target is aggressive but plausible; can you clarify what test harness you plan to use and whether that includes cold‑start times?
- For quality acceptance: can we add an exclusion for documented edge cases (we'll provide a list) so they don't count toward the core recall metric?

I'll review the CSV late today and route to Tara. Tue/Wed call works — I'm available Tue 10–11am PT.

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@caspianhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance criteria & MAP: Caspian Health pilot checkpoints

Hi Emily / Marcus —

Following up after Marcus's MAP: I pulled the acceptance_test_matrix into a slightly expanded verification runbook and added who on the Redwood side will execute each step (ops, SRE, or solutions). Highlights below and a few clarifications inline in the sheet.

Verification highlights (short):
- Smoke test (Week 1): 100 synthetic requests across expected payload sizes; verify cold + warm latencies. Pass if median < 150ms and 95th < 350ms. Failure triggers investigation and a one-week remediation plan.
- Mid‑pilot (Week 3): Run the curated eval set (n=1,200 labeled cases from Caspian). Pass if recall >= 85% on core cases (exclusions flagged) and false positive rate < 12%.
- Acceptance run (Week 5): 72‑hour continuous run using real traffic snapshot; measure throughput, error budget, and stability. Pass requires sustained SLOs for 72 hours.
- Security evidence: We will provide SOC2 Type II report, a Network Isolation one‑pager, and a KMS integration note (stub). Procurement packet will be delivered to the procurement email address on approval.

Two practical items:
1) Cold starts: our latency numbers in the MAP assume a warm cache. For fairness, we'll include a cold‑start column in the runbook and mark it informational unless you need cold starts included in the exit gate.
2) Edge cases: please send the exclusion list in a simple CSV; we'll tag them in the evaluation and exclude from the pass/fail metric per your ask.

I've attached: acceptance_test_matrix.csv (updated), verification_runbook_v1.pdf (summary).

Attachment stubs: [Attachment: acceptance_test_matrix.csv (updated)] [Attachment: verification_runbook_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Next steps: Marcus to schedule the Tuesday 10am PT alignment call (Emily proposed). On that call we'll confirm names for each test owner, finalize the exclusion list, and lock the dates.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
